question: During an assisted vaginal breech delivery, Lovset's manoeuvre is used to deliver the extended arms by rotating the baby's trunk to bring each arm into the hollow of the sacrum before sweeping it across the face.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement accurately describes Lovset's manoeuvre. The key principle is rotation of the trunk to bring the posterior arm into the roomier sacral hollow before delivering each arm in sequence. Review the breech delivery section.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Lovset's manoeuvre exploits the oblique diameter of the pelvis. The trunk is rotated 180° (keeping the back uppermost) so that the posterior arm becomes anterior and enters the sacral hollow, where it can be swept down. This is the standard manoeuvre for extended arms in breech delivery.
